summary: Upshur County, TX Texas Forest Service tower completed by May 1962 (87-ft steel); 1968 and 1972 newspaper items; the Texas index lists it gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no removal date or site description found

events.note: Texas Forest Service announced the completed tower in a May 3, 1962 Gilmer Mirror report; built on land leased from a Longview owner
Named at opening: crewleader Leon B. Patrick of Longview and crewman Bennie Wood of Diana
Two Longview boys tried for burglarizing the tower on October 7 (year inferred from 'last Oct. 7' in the January 25, 1968 report); a jury found them not guilty
Thieves broke into the tower twice; a short-wave radio, binoculars and a coffee pot were taken (Feb. 3, 1972 report)

evidence.supports: Site heading: Upshur County, Texas Forest Service
Tower completed and announced in May 1962
evidence.quote: A forest fire lookout tower has been completed at East Mountain

evidence.supports: Tower erected on land leased to the Texas Forest Service
evidence.quote: The tower was erected on land leased to the Texas Forest Service by Mrs. Judith O'Byrne Adams of Longview.
Operation of the 87-foot steel girder structure is the responsibility of crewleader Leon B. Patrick, Longview.

evidence.supports: Crewman named as Bennie Wood of Diana
evidence.quote: His crewman is Bennie Wood of Diana.

evidence.supports: Tower was to work with Texas Forest Service towers at Hallsville, Gilmont, Latch and Meadows
evidence.quote: Chestnut states the new tower will work in cooperation with other Texas Forest Service towers located at Hallsville, Gilmont, Latch and Meadows.

evidence.supports: January 1968 jury verdict of not guilty in the burglary of the tower
evidence.quote: A district court jury took just twenty minutes Tuesday to find two 15-year-old Longview boys not guilty of burglarizing the East Mountain fire tower last Oct. 7.

evidence.supports: February 1972 thefts: short-wave radio, binoculars and coffee pot
evidence.quote: Thieves have broken into the East Mountain Fire Lookout tower twice recently, taking a heavy short wave radio, binoculars and a coffee pot, among other things

evidence.supports: Texas index lists the tower as Tower, Gone
Report dated January 25, 1968 (jury verdict on a Tuesday)

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page heads the site 'Upshur County - Texas Forest Service' and the 1962 clip names Upshur County; 'Upshire' is a misspelling carried into the index

sources.title: East Mountain
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (centraluslookouts.weebly.com), quoting The Gilmer Mirror

notes_for_editor: Built, staffed and incident dates come from Forest Lookouts clippings of The Gilmer Mirror (1962, 1968, 1972); the newspapers themselves were not read. The 1968 report says 'last Oct. 7', so the October date is 1967 by inference. The 87-foot figure is the structure height as stated; the source does not say whether it runs to the cab floor, so height_m 26.5 (the brief's value, consistent with 87 ft) should be checked. No removal date, sale or site description found after 2 WebSearch calls and about 4 page reads. The Gilmont page (a neighboring TFS tower) turned up in search but was not used. The brief's county 'Upshire' is corrected to Upshur.
